title: akitaonrails/ai-memory: shared long-term memory across coding agents
friendlyTitle: ai-memory helps different coding agents remember the same project
summary: ai-memory is a Rust-based memory layer designed to preserve project knowledge and hand work between coding-agent command-line tools from different vendors. The MIT-licensed project has about 7,600 stars and gained 217 stars on GitHub Trending today.
friendlySummary: ai-memory saves useful project knowledge so coding agents can continue work across sessions or hand it to another agent. It gained 217 stars on GitHub today.
whyItMatters: Developers can retain decisions, observations and useful context when changing agents or starting fresh sessions instead of repeatedly rebuilding the same understanding. Treat stored memories as maintained project data: inspect them, remove stale claims and avoid capturing secrets.
friendlyWhyItMatters: It can reduce repeated explanations when you change tools or restart a session. Review old memories regularly and do not save passwords or other secrets.
